onenight.title: Une nuit
onenight.kicker: One night ashore · pick the quarter you are berthed nearest · walking order
onenight.lede: Paris dines at eight or later, and most bistro kitchens stop taking orders between ten and half past; the brasseries and the bouillons run to midnight. Each quarter below is one evening, in the order you walk it: the apéro, the table, the late room. Every name opens its full card; hours were re-checked on 16 October 2026, and where the listings disagree the step says call.
onenight.door_en: Crew ashore for one evening: a plan for each quarter — the apéro, the bistro, the counter and the late room, in walking order.
onenight.door_note: L’apéro · le bistrot · la table · la nuit

quarters.name: The 11th · Charonne to Oberkampf
quarters.line: The neo-bistro's own wine bar, the raw bar that never books, and a dance floor after eleven.

steps.name: Septime La Cave
steps.text: A glass on rue Basfroi before the pavement crowd arrives. No bookings; listed daily 16:00–23:00, but listings vary.

steps.name: Clamato
steps.text: Round the corner on rue de Charonne, be there at the opening for a stool: oysters, the razor clams in herb butter, whatever the morning brought. It never takes bookings; a 2026 listing gives Tuesday to Saturday, others differ, so call.

steps.name: Bambino
steps.text: Fifteen minutes north to rue Saint-Sébastien, where the listening bar's dining room turns into a dance floor late in the evening.

quarters.after: Spend more: [[venue:v-septime|Septime]] next door to Clamato, booked online about three weeks out, in its first season since Bertrand Grébaut's death. Quieter: [[card:Notre Dame Music Bar|Notre Dame Music Bar]], early on a weekday.

quarters.name: Canal Saint-Martin · the 10th
quarters.line: Where the cave à manger began, then jazz in the room of 1981.

steps.name: Le Verre Volé
steps.text: Dinner among the bottles on rue de Lancry, a minute from the canal. Book for dinner; listings disagree on its hours, so check when you reserve.

steps.name: New Morning
steps.text: Fifteen minutes west to rue des Petites-Écuries for the night's concert; doors open around 20:00–20:30, so check the programme and buy ahead.

quarters.after: Earlier and cheaper: the canal itself at dusk ([[card:Canal Saint-Martin|its card]]), or a drink on the basin at [[card:Le Pavillon des Canaux|Le Pavillon des Canaux]], open to midnight midweek.

quarters.name: Belleville
quarters.line: The view from the top of the park, then the blackboard Raquel Carena has cooked since 1987.

steps.name: Belleville at dusk
steps.text: Climb to the terrace of the Parc de Belleville for the city spread out below you at the end of the afternoon.

steps.name: Le Baratin
steps.text: Down to rue Jouye-Rouve for the offal-forward blackboard and the natural cellar. Book by phone a day or two ahead; dinner Tuesday to Saturday by an undated Time Out listing, closed Sunday and Monday.

quarters.after: After dinner: the roof at [[card:Le Perchoir Ménilmontant|Le Perchoir]], down the hill in Ménilmontant; its open roof is seasonal, so check before you climb.

quarters.name: Saint-Germain and the Latin Quarter
quarters.line: The terrace facing the oldest church, the crémerie of 1845, and swing in a medieval cellar.

steps.name: Les Deux Magots
steps.text: A glass on the terrace facing Saint-Germain-des-Prés; open daily to about 1:00.

steps.name: Polidor
steps.text: Ten minutes to rue Monsieur-le-Prince for the boeuf bourguignon and the chocolate mousse at shared tables. Hours differ between listings, so call.

steps.name: Caveau de la Huchette
steps.text: Across the boulevard Saint-Michel to the jazz cellar: music from 21:30, the floor fullest after 23:00 on a Friday or Saturday.

quarters.after: Spend more: [[venue:v-brasserie-lipp|Brasserie Lipp]] for the choucroute; book for a weekend evening. Grander for one drink: [[card:Bar Joséphine|Bar Joséphine]] at the Lutetia.

quarters.name: The Marais
quarters.line: The royal square at dusk, a galette done properly, jazz at Châtelet.

steps.name: Place des Vosges
steps.text: Walk the arcades of the square of 1612 as the lamps come on; it is free and always open.

steps.name: Breizh Café
steps.text: Ten minutes to rue Vieille du Temple for the galette complète and a bowl of cider. Reserve; listings disagree on the days, so check.

steps.name: Duc des Lombards
steps.text: Fifteen minutes west to rue des Lombards for the late set, or the jam after it.

quarters.after: Cheaper: [[venue:v-l-as-du-fallafel|L'As du Fallafel]] on rue des Rosiers, but not on a Friday evening or a Saturday (closed for the Sabbath). Spend more: [[venue:v-datil|Datil]] in the 3rd, booked ahead.

quarters.name: Opéra and the Grands Boulevards
quarters.line: A free roof over the opera's dome, then the bouillon of 1896.

steps.name: Galeries Lafayette terrace
steps.text: Up to the eighth-floor terrace for the Palais Garnier's roof at eye level. It keeps the store's hours: in winter, go an hour before the 19:30 close.

steps.name: Bouillon Chartier
steps.text: Fifteen minutes east to the faubourg Montmartre: no reservations, so queue for the oeuf mayonnaise and the bourguignon. Open daily to midnight.

quarters.after: The same idea at the top of the hill: [[venue:v-bouillon-pigalle|Bouillon Pigalle]] on the boulevard de Clichy, open daily to midnight.

quarters.name: Montparnasse
quarters.line: The painters' café that stays up late, then the Art Deco hall and its curry.

steps.name: Le Sélect
steps.text: A glass at a marble table on the boulevard du Montparnasse; open daily from early morning to about 2:00.

steps.name: La Coupole
steps.text: Across the boulevard to the hall of 1927, its pillars painted by artists, for the lamb curry served since opening. Book: it gets very busy.

quarters.after: Cheaper: the galette at [[venue:v-la-creperie-de-josselin|La Crêperie de Josselin]] on rue du Montparnasse, not re-confirmed this autumn: call.

quarters.name: The 7th · by the Invalides
quarters.line: The river at dusk, then the Basque canteen and its basin of rice pudding.

steps.name: Parc Rives de Seine
steps.text: Walk the car-free quay below the Musée d'Orsay as the light goes.

steps.name: Chez L'Ami Jean
steps.text: Twenty minutes west to rue Malar: game in season, and the riz au lait for the table. Book well ahead; Tuesday to Saturday by a May 2026 listing.

quarters.after: The grand version, for lunch on a weekday: [[venue:v-l-arpege|L'Arpège]] on rue de Varenne, booked well ahead.

getaway.title: Le week-end
getaway.door_en: Friday night to Sunday afternoon: the island at dusk and a Left Bank brasserie, the market and the railway garden, the jewel box, a Belleville blackboard, and a Sunday of organic stalls, Rodin's roses and a café terrace.
getaway.door_note: L’île · le marché · la Sainte-Chapelle · le bistrot
getaway.kicker: The getaway weekend · Friday night to Sunday afternoon
getaway.lede: Paris sells itself as a terrace on the Champs-Élysées, a table with the tower in view and a queue at the museum. The real weekend is the market, the bistro and the walk between them: the tip of the island at dusk on Friday, the Marché d'Aligre before noon on Saturday, a railway viaduct turned garden, the Sainte-Chapelle's glass in the afternoon, dinner at a blackboard in Belleville, and a Sunday of organic stalls, roses and a long lunch on the boulevard. Every stop below is already in this guide and was re-checked on 16 October 2026; where a place could not be re-confirmed, the stop says so. This reading puts them in order, and tells you what to book before you fly.
book: [[venue:v-brasserie-lipp|Brasserie Lipp]] — a table for Friday night; walk-ins are risky on busy evenings.
[[venue:v-le-baratin|Le Baratin]] — Saturday dinner, by phone, a day or two ahead.
[[card:Sainte-Chapelle|The Sainte-Chapelle]] — a ticket for Saturday afternoon: EUR 22 for visitors from outside the EEA (Oct 2026); allow time for the law-courts security gate.
[[venue:v-chez-l-ami-jean|Chez L'Ami Jean]] — if you stay on into Tuesday, the dinner people book weeks out.

days.label: Friday
days.title: The island at dusk, the Left Bank at night

stops.name: The willow at the tip of the island
stops.text: Down the steps behind Henri IV's statue on the Pont Neuf to the point of the Île de la Cité, with the river splitting round you.
stops.meta: Île de la Cité, steps from the Pont Neuf · free · it can flood when the Seine runs high

stops.name: Choucroute at Brasserie Lipp
stops.text: Fifteen minutes across the Pont Neuf and up the rue de Seine to the boulevard: the choucroute garnie, the house dish since 1880, in the listed 1900 room.
stops.meta: 151 boulevard Saint-Germain · listings give daily to about 00:45 or later · book for weekend evenings

stops.name: Swing at the Caveau de la Huchette
stops.text: Ten minutes east to the medieval cellar on rue de la Huchette, where the dancers come late.
stops.meta: Rue de la Huchette, 5th · music from 21:30 · fullest after 23:00 at the weekend

days.label: Saturday
days.title: The market, the viaduct, the glass and the blackboard

stops.name: The Marché d'Aligre
stops.text: The least touristy market in central Paris: the street stalls, the covered Beauvau hall and the flea market on one square.
stops.meta: Place d'Aligre, 12th · stalls Sat 7:30–14:30 · closed Monday

stops.name: The Coulée verte
stops.text: Climb onto the old railway viaduct by the avenue Daumesnil and walk the garden along its top, above the street.
stops.meta: Behind the Opéra Bastille · from 09:00 at weekends · closes earlier in winter

stops.name: Lunch under the glass dome at Bofinger
stops.text: Back to the Bastille for the Alsatian brasserie of 1864: the choucroute de la mer under the Art Nouveau dome.
stops.meta: 5–7 rue de la Bastille · daily lunch 12:00–15:00 (May 2026 listing) · confirm

stops.name: The Sainte-Chapelle
stops.text: Metro to the Cité for Louis IX's chapel of 1248, its windows some fifteen metres tall, leaving almost no wall.
stops.meta: Boulevard du Palais · daily from 09:00, to 17:00 October to March · EUR 22 outside the EEA (Oct 2026)

stops.name: The arcades of the Place des Vosges
stops.text: Twenty minutes east through the Marais to the square of 1612, walking its arcades as the day goes.

stops.name: A glass at Septime La Cave
stops.text: Fifteen minutes to rue Basfroi for a natural glass before dinner, standing if the room is full.
stops.meta: 3 rue Basfroi, 11th · no bookings · listed daily 16:00–23:00 (listings vary)

stops.name: Dinner at Le Baratin
stops.text: Metro up to Belleville for Raquel Carena's blackboard: the calf's brain in lemon butter if it is on, and the cellar's pick by the glass.
stops.meta: 3 rue Jouye-Rouve, 20th · Sat 19:30–23:00 by an undated Time Out listing · book by phone

days.label: Sunday
days.title: The organic market, the food hall, the roses and the terrace

stops.name: The Sunday organic market on the boulevard Raspail
stops.text: The best-known organic market in Paris, under the plane trees of the boulevard.
stops.meta: Boulevard Raspail, 6th · Sunday 9:00–15:00 by Paris je t'aime (one city page says 7:00–14:30)

stops.name: La Grande Épicerie
stops.text: Two minutes away, Le Bon Marché's food hall for what the market did not have: the cheese, the butter, a bottle for the galley.

stops.name: Rodin's roses
stops.text: Fifteen minutes west to rue de Varenne: The Thinker among the clipped box and the rose beds, the dome of the Invalides over the wall.
stops.meta: 77 rue de Varenne · Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 · closing times differ between listings

stops.name: Lunch on the terrace of the Café de Flore
stops.text: Back to the boulevard Saint-Germain for a croque-monsieur and the long Sunday watch from the terrace.

stops.name: The car-free quay
stops.text: Down to the river below the Musée d'Orsay and walk the quay east until it is time to go.
stops.meta: Left bank below the Musée d'Orsay · free

more.title: If you have only one evening
more.text: Take the Saint-Germain plan in One Night: a glass at [[card:Les Deux Magots|Les Deux Magots]], the bourguignon at [[venue:v-polidor|Polidor]], and the cellar at [[card:Caveau de la Huchette|the Caveau de la Huchette]], all inside twenty minutes' walk.

more.title: The grand night instead
more.text: Swap a dinner for one of the three-star houses, booked as soon as the dates are fixed: [[venue:v-plenitude-cheval-blanc-paris|Plénitude]] on the Seine, [[venue:v-kei|Kei]] by the Louvre, or [[venue:v-l-arpege|L'Arpège]] at a weekday lunch (it is closed at the weekend). [[venue:v-table-by-bruno-verjus|Table]] serves its last dinner on 22 December 2026.

more.title: This October and November
items: [[card:Art Basel Paris, 23–25 October|Art Basel Paris]] at the Grand Palais, public days Friday 23 to Sunday 25 October.
[[card:The clocks go back, Sunday 25 October|The clocks go back]] on Sunday 25 October: the evening walks get dark an hour earlier.
[[card:Salon du Chocolat, 28 October–1 November|The Salon du Chocolat]], Wednesday 28 October to Sunday 1 November, Porte de Versailles.
[[card:Giverny|Giverny]] closes for the winter after 1 November.
[[card:Beaujolais Nouveau, Thursday 19 November|Beaujolais Nouveau]] on Thursday 19 November.

more.title: Where to sleep
more.text: This guide does not review hotels. The four it names are there for a drink, not a room: the Ritz ([[card:Bar Hemingway|Bar Hemingway]]), [[card:Le Bar du Bristol|Le Bristol]], the Lutetia ([[card:Bar Joséphine|Bar Joséphine]]) and Cheval Blanc ([[card:Le Tout-Paris|Le Tout-Paris]]). We have not judged their rooms.

more.title: What we would leave out
more.text: The terraces of the Champs-Élysées, any table sold on its Eiffel Tower view, and the man on the pavement with a photo menu: the guide's own warnings are under [[card:Champs-Élysées terraces|What to skip]]. And the Marché des Enfants Rouges, which burned on the night of 11 to 12 October 2026: [[card:Marché des Enfants Rouges|its card]] has the news.
